comments.headline: Building elevations and sections missing; vertical clearances unverified
comments.summary: The site plan lacks building elevation sheets and section/profile views necessary to verify vertical clearances from surveyed overhead conductor elevations to buildings and their projections. This documentation is required by code when buildings are within clearance distance of overhead facilities.
comments.attn: Applicant must hire registered professional surveyor to provide measured pole and conductor elevation data.

details.text: No building elevation sheets included in the 39-sheet site plan set. Surveyed overhead conductor elevations and dimensioned clearances to building faces are required to verify 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance when buildings are within potential clearance distance of overhead facilities.

runComments.comment: No building elevation sheets are included in the 39-sheet site plan set. Building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevations and dimensioned clearances are required to demonstrate compliance with clearance requirements when buildings are within potential clearance distance of overhead facilities.

No building elevation sheets are included in the site plan package showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations and locations. The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows utility pole locations but provides no conductor elevation data. Building elevation sheets with registered surveyor data showing conductor heights and clearance dimensions to building faces and projections are required to verify vertical clearance compliance. Provide building elevations with surveyed conductor elevation callouts.

No building elevation sheets are included in this site plan set. Surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors required to demonstrate clearances are not provided on any available document.

details.text: Building projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, canopies) near overhead conductors lack elevation documentation showing vertical relationship and clearance dimensions. Both 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances from building projections to outside conductors must be verified on elevation views.

runComments.comment: No building elevation sheets are provided showing building projections relative to overhead conductors. Without elevation views detailing overhang, awning, balcony, or roof projections and their clearances from overhead lines, compliance with both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances cannot be verified.

No building elevation views are provided showing the vertical relationship between building projections and overhead electric conductors. Site plan (Sheet 9) and electrical plan (Sheet 21) show OHE lines and building footprints but lack elevation views documenting clearances. Both 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances from building projections to outside conductor must be verified. Provide building elevation sheets with surveyed conductor elevations and dimension callouts showing clearances from all building projections.

details.text: No section or profile views provided showing dimensions from outer electric conductor to outermost edge of buildings and building projections. Site plan and electrical plan show buildings near overhead lines but lack dimensioned clearance verification exhibits required by code.

runComments.comment: No section or profile views are provided showing dimensions from the outer electric conductor to the outermost edge of buildings and building projections. Site plan shows buildings near overhead lines but lacks dimensioned clearance verification exhibits required by code.

Section and profile views with dimension callouts from the outside conductor to building edges are absent from the site plan. Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) references 'See Sht. 19 for Profile' but Sheet 19 is a water/wastewater utility tap plan, not electrical clearance profiles. No dimension lines originating at conductor locations and extending to outermost building edges are provided on any sheet. Provide section/profile exhibits with specific clearance dimensions from outside conductor to all building faces and projections.

Section and profile views showing dimensions from the outer electric conductor to outermost building edges are not provided on the site plan. While a site plan drawing exists, it contains only plan-view (top-down) information with no vertical section views depicting conductor-to-building clearances.

comments.headline: Clearance dimensions and measurement methodology not documented on plans
comments.summary: No clearance dimensions are shown on any site plan sheets demonstrating measurements from the outside conductor to buildings, structures, driveways, or other site features. The measurement standard (from outside conductor, not pole centerline) cannot be verified because no dimensions are present.
comments.attn: Dimension lines must originate at conductor location, not pole center. Multi-conductor installations have conductors offset several feet from pole center.

details.text: No clearance dimensions shown on any plan sheets from the outside conductor to buildings, structures, walls, or other site features. Measurement standard (from outside conductor, not pole centerline) cannot be verified because no dimensions are shown. Distance dimensions from buildings to property boundary (29.6', 45.9', 21.3') are not clearance dimensions from the overhead electric conductor.

runComments.comment: No clearance dimensions are provided on any site plan sheets showing measurements from the outside conductor (outermost electric line) to buildings, structures, walls, or other site features. Where clearance dimensions should be shown (such as on building elevation sheets or section views), none are present. The measurement standard (from outside conductor, not from pole centerline) cannot be verified because no dimensions are shown.

Critical requirement: all clearance dimensions must be measured from the OUTSIDE CONDUCTOR, never from utility pole centerline. Multi-conductor installations have conductors offset several feet from pole center. Currently, no clearance dimensions are shown on any plan sheets, so this measurement methodology cannot be verified. When clearance dimensions are provided, ensure dimension lines originate at the conductor location (not pole center) and extend to the outermost edge of the site feature being cleared.

Site plan shows distance dimensions from buildings to property boundary (29.6', 45.9', 21.3'), but these are NOT clearance dimensions from the overhead electric conductor. Code requires clearance dimensions measured from the outside conductor, not from the property boundary or utility pole centerline. The overhead conductor location is not dimensioned relative to these distance measurements.

details.text: 15-foot radial clearance requirement for distribution facilities not documented with any clearance dimensions, measurements, or profile/section views. Clearance applicability cannot be determined without conductor voltage labeling and three-dimensional clearance verification from outside conductors to buildings, parking areas, and other customer facilities.

runComments.comment: The 15-foot radial clearance requirement applies to all customer facilities. No profile, section, or elevation views are provided showing radial clearance measurements from outside conductors to building footprints, parking areas, or other site features in three dimensions.

Overhead electric lines (OHE) are shown on plans but are not labeled with voltage classification. The 15-foot radial clearance requirement applies only to distribution facilities operating below 60kV (typically 12.47kV or 34.5kV in Austin). Without voltage labeling, the applicability of this distribution-specific requirement cannot be determined. Verify whether shown OHE lines are distribution or transmission facilities and label with operating voltage on utility plans.

Overhead distribution line present on site plan, but no clearance dimensions or radial clearance verification provided. No horizontal plan details showing 15-foot radial clearance from outside conductor to any customer facilities or site features.

comments.headline: Clearance from buildings and retaining walls to overhead conductors unverified
comments.summary: Site plan shows buildings and retaining walls near overhead electric facilities, but no surveyed dimension callouts demonstrate compliance with 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from outside conductors to building faces, walls, and edges. Walls up to 14 feet high are proposed near OHE lines without clearance documentation.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy coordination on right-of-way facilities clearances.

details.text: Buildings proposed near Valley View Road right-of-way where existing overhead electric facilities are shown. Plans contain general Austin Energy boilerplate notes but do not document that specific 7.5-foot horizontal and 15-foot radial clearances from OHE to buildings in the ROW-adjacent area have been verified and met with dimension callouts.

runComments.comment: Overhead electric facilities exist in the ROW adjacent to the site (along Valley View Road, western boundary). Buildings are proposed on site, but surveyed clearance dimensions from buildings to these facilities are not provided on elevation or section views to demonstrate permanent clearance requirements are met.

Buildings are proposed near Valley View Road where existing overhead electric facilities are shown. Plans contain general Austin Energy boilerplate notes acknowledging responsibility for maintaining clearances but do not document that specific 7.5-foot horizontal and 15-foot radial clearances from OHE to buildings in the ROW-adjacent area have been verified and met. Provide dimension callouts on site plan and building elevations demonstrating compliance with both clearance envelopes from OHE to each building edge within potential clearance distance of ROW facilities.

details.text: Retaining walls up to 14 feet height proposed on southern and eastern boundaries near overhead lines. No section views or clearance dimension callouts from outer electric conductor to wall faces provided. Minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from conductor to outermost wall edge must be documented in cross-section with dimension annotations.

runComments.comment: Retaining walls are proposed on the site (up to 14 feet height per Sheet 38). Walls are shown on the site plan near the southern and eastern property boundaries where overhead lines exist. However, no section views showing vertical clearance dimensions from the outer electric line conductor to the wall faces are provided to verify the 7.5-foot clearance requirement.

Site plan (Sheet 9) and wall plan sheets show retaining walls at multiple locations on the site near OHE lines, but no clearance dimension callouts demonstrate the 7.5-foot minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from outermost conductor to wall face. Provide dimension annotations on site plan and wall section sheets showing clearance from outside conductor to outermost edge of retaining wall.

details.text: Wall section exhibits showing structural details do not include dimension callouts from outside conductor of overhead electric lines to outermost edge of retaining wall faces. Clearance verification dimensions from conductor location to wall are required on all section views.

runComments.comment: Retaining walls are proposed near overhead electric lines on the southern and eastern boundaries. Section exhibits showing dimensions from outer electric conductor to the outermost edge of wall faces for clearance verification are not provided. Wall sections show structural details but lack clearance dimension callouts referencing conductor locations.

Wall plan (Sheets 38 and 39) shows retaining wall section views and details but these cross-sections do not include dimension callouts from the outside conductor of overhead electric lines to the outermost edge of retaining wall faces. Section views showing clearance dimensions from conductor to wall are required for compliance verification. Provide section views of all retaining walls with clearance dimension annotations from outside conductor location.

comments.headline: Vehicle parking and driveway vertical clearances to overhead lines not documented
comments.summary: Grading plan shows driveway and parking area elevations, but no cross-section views document vertical clearance from finished surface to lowest point of overhead electric conductors. Required clearances are 16 feet for parking without truck traffic, 18 feet with truck traffic, and 12 feet minimum for residential pedestrian areas; 30 feet minimum for transmission lines.
comments.crossDep: Coordination with site grading engineer and Austin Energy on transmission line clearances.
comments.attn: Verify whether truck traffic is expected on driveways to determine 16-foot vs. 18-foot requirement.

details.text: Driveway and parking area elevations shown on grading plan, but no registered surveyor mid-span clearance measurements provided showing lowest point of overhead conductors (including attached equipment) relative to driveway and parking surface elevations. No section views with dimension callouts document clearance distances; determination of truck traffic use and resulting 16-foot vs. 18-foot requirement not explicitly documented.

runComments.comment: Driveways and parking areas are proposed throughout the site. Grading plan shows finished floor elevations for buildings and finished grade in parking areas. However, no surveyed mid-span clearance measurements are provided showing the lowest point of overhead lines (including any attached equipment) relative to driveway and parking surface elevations. Determination of whether truck traffic will use driveways to establish 16-foot vs. 18-foot requirement is not explicitly documented.

Grading plan (Sheet 11) and site plan (Sheet 9) show driveway alignments and elevations, but no cross-section views document vertical clearance from finished driveway surface to lowest point of overhead electric conductors (including telecommunications attachments). The 16-foot minimum clearance (parking without truck traffic) or 18-foot clearance (areas with truck traffic) must be verified through section views with dimension callouts. Provide section views showing driveway finished grade elevation and overhead line clearance dimensions; verify whether truck traffic is expected.

While the grading plan (Sheet 11) shows driveway locations and elevations, no section views showing vertical clearances from the overhead electric line to the driveway surface are provided. Mid-span clearance verification required by code is not documented.

details.text: Parking pad surface elevations shown on plans, but no section views document vertical clearance from parking pad elevation to overhead electric lines. Clearance dimensions from parking surface to lowest conductor point must be documented; 16 feet for parking without truck traffic, 18 feet with truck traffic. No plan note documents the required clearance or identifies truck traffic expectation.

runComments.comment: Site plan shows parking areas and driveways, and grading plan shows finished surface elevations, but no section views document vertical clearance from parking pad surface to overhead electric lines. Plans must include section views with dimension callouts showing clearance from parking pad elevation to lowest overhead conductor point (16 feet for parking without truck traffic, 18 feet with truck traffic, 12 feet minimum for residential pedestrian areas). Additionally, a note on plans must identify the clearance requirement. Provide section views with vertical clearance dimensions and a plan note documenting required clearance.

details.text: Transmission notes on Sheet 3 indicate transmission facilities present. Grading plan shows driveway and road surface elevations, but no section views document 30-foot minimum vertical clearance from road/driveway surface to electric transmission lines. Transmission line locations and easement boundaries not clearly delineated on plans.

runComments.comment: Sheet 3, Block 9 indicates transmission facilities are present and notes restrictions for areas within 25 feet of transmission structures. Grading plan shows driveway and road surface elevations but provides no section views documenting 30-foot minimum vertical clearance from road/driveway surface to electric transmission lines. Verify transmission line locations, provide transmission easement boundary on plans, and provide section views showing road/driveway elevation with vertical clearance dimension to transmission lines (minimum 30 feet).

comments.headline: Proposed trees near overhead lines lack utility compatibility verification
comments.summary: Landscape plan shows 3 mitigation trees and other plantings within 10–50 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors and potentially near transmission lines. Trees within 10 lateral feet of distribution (or 50 lateral feet of transmission) must be from ECM Appendix F Utility Compatible Shade Trees list, marked 'UC', generally with mature height ≤20 feet. No verification provided that Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, and Texas Mountain Laurel meet this requirement.
comments.crossDep: City Arborist office for utility compatibility verification and ECM Appendix F standard.
comments.attn: Verify all tree species against ECM Appendix F Utility Compatible Shade Trees list. Relocate non-compatible trees outside clearance zones or specify approved compatible replacement species.

details.text: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows 3 mitigation trees marked 'M' and additional plantings (Parking Lot Trees marked 'PL', other ornamentals) within 10–50 lateral feet of overhead distribution line at southern property boundary. Plant list (Sheets 31–32) identifies species as Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, and Texas Mountain Laurel, but does not explicitly verify any species are marked 'UC' (utility-compatible) in ECM Appendix F or confirm mature heights ≤20 feet. No species identification provided specifically for the 3 mitigation trees near OHE.

runComments.comment: Landscape plan shows 3 mitigation trees (marked 'M') positioned within 10 lateral feet of the overhead electric line (-OHE-) on the southern property boundary. UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires trees within 50 lateral feet of transmission lines (or 10 lateral feet of distribution lines) to be from the Utility Compatible Shade Trees list (ECM Appendix F, species marked UC with mature height generally ≤20 feet). The plant list (Sheet 35) identifies proposed shade trees as Live Oak and Cedar Elm, and ornamental trees as Texas Mountain Laurel and Mexican Redbud, but does not explicitly verify that any of these species are marked utility-compatible or that the specific 3 mitigation trees near the overhead line are one of these approved species. No species identification is provided for the 3 mitigation trees shown on the landscape plan near the overhead lines.

Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows trees in proximity to overhead electric line (OHE) running along southern and eastern boundaries, identified only by classification codes (M, SY, PL) without species identification. No lateral distances from trees to conductors are documented. Trees within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors (or 50 lateral feet of transmission conductors) must be from the Utility Compatible Shade Trees list (ECM Appendix F, species marked 'UC', generally mature height ≤20 feet). Provide tree species identification on landscape plan by reference to plant schedule (Sheet 32 or detailed plant list), verify species against ECM Appendix F utility-compatible list, and document lateral distances from trees to OHE. Relocate any non-compatible trees outside the clearance zones.

Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows proposed trees (Mitigation Trees marked 'M' and Parking Lot Trees marked 'PL') located within 10-50 feet lateral distance from the existing overhead electric distribution line at the southern property boundary. No documentation provided verifying that these proposed tree species (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel) are included in ECM Appendix F 'Utility Compatible Shade Trees' list marked 'UC'. Plant list does not reference ECM Appendix F utility-compatible designation for any species.

comments.headline: Utility pole locations and down guy wire clearances not addressed; easements missing
comments.summary: Existing survey shows utility poles and down guy wires supporting overhead distribution lines. Site plan does not explicitly address pole relocation, driveway conflicts, or down guy anchor locations and required easements (10-foot width, 5-foot extension beyond anchor). Sidewalk clearances from poles at property limits not verified. Transmission structure down guy anchor easements also not documented.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy coordination on pole relocation, down guy anchor locations, and easement designations.
comments.attn: Applicant must coordinate with Austin Energy to verify existing pole and down guy anchor locations and confirm relocations or easement dedications. Down guy locations not clearly visible on survey may still require easement documentation.

details.text: Existing survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles along western property boundary. Site plan shows driveway alignments, but no notes or dimension callouts address whether existing poles within or immediately adjacent to driveway alignments conflict or require relocation. If poles are within proposed driveway envelope, minimum 30-foot setback from driveway edge is required.

runComments.comment: Site plan shows internal driveways and parking layout. Overhead utility poles (part of OHE line configuration) exist on the site. The plan does not explicitly show pole relocation or notes indicating whether poles within 30 feet of driveway edges have been relocated. Without surveyed pole locations and driveway alignment dimensions, conflict determination cannot be definitively made.

Existing survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles along the western property boundary near Valley View Road. Site plan (Sheet 9) shows driveway alignments, but no notes or dimensions address whether existing poles are in conflict with driveways or require relocation. If existing poles are within or immediately adjacent to proposed driveway alignments, poles must be relocated minimum 30 feet from driveway edge. Provide dimension callouts showing pole locations relative to driveway edges, or provide relocation notes if poles will be moved.

details.text: Existing survey shows utility poles along Valley View Road frontage. Site plan shows sidewalk alignments along property boundary. No dimension callouts or notes verify that sidewalks are cleared from existing power poles at each end of property along right-of-way. Distance from sidewalk edges to pole locations at north and south property limits not documented.

runComments.comment: Existing survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles along Valley View Road frontage. Site plan shows sidewalk alignments along the property boundary. However, no dimension callouts or notes verify that sidewalks are cleared from existing power poles at each end of the property along right-of-way. Provide dimension annotations on site plan showing distance from sidewalk edges to pole locations at north and south property limits, or provide relocation/adjustment notes if poles are in conflict.

details.text: Existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles with guy wire symbols indicating down guy presence. However, site plan does not address whether down guys are in conflict with proposed accessible paths, driveways, or other site features, or whether they have been relocated or poles converted to self-supporting structures. Down guy wire locations and their relationship to proposed site features not explicitly mapped or resolved.

runComments.comment: Down guy wires from distribution poles may exist on the site but are not clearly depicted on the survey or site plan. The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) includes a legend item for 'guy wires' but the plan view does not explicitly show down guy wire locations or their relationship to proposed accessible paths and driveways. Without explicit down guy location mapping, potential conflicts cannot be definitively identified or resolved. Electric utility infrastructure, including guy wire systems, is frequently omitted from site plans per the grouping's common violation patterns.

Existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles with guy wire symbols (support cables from poles to ground anchors), indicating down guy presence. However, site plan does not address whether down guys are in conflict with proposed accessible paths, driveways, or other site features, or whether they have been relocated or poles converted to self-supporting structures. Down guy wires and anchor locations must be verified against all proposed site features and either relocated or resolved through pole conversion. Provide down guy relocation notes or conversion specifications for any poles with down guys that conflict with site improvements.

details.text: Existing survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles with guy wire symbols indicating down guy anchors from distribution poles. Site plan and easement exhibit (Sheet 2) do not show dedicated down guy anchor easements (10-foot wide with minimum 5-foot extension past ground entry point of each anchor). Down guy anchor locations not explicitly mapped or dimensioned on any plan sheet.

runComments.comment: Down guy anchor locations (if they exist) are not explicitly mapped on the site plan or easement exhibits. The survey legend includes guy wire symbols but these are not clearly identified on the survey drawing. Without explicit down guy anchor point locations with associated 10-foot-wide and 5-foot-extension easement boundaries shown on an easement exhibit, compliance with this documentation requirement cannot be verified.

Existing survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles with guy wire symbols indicating down guy anchors. Site plan and easement exhibit must show dedicated down guy anchor easements (10-foot wide extending minimum 5 feet past ground entry point of anchor) for each down guy anchor visible on survey. If down guys are relocated or removed, provide relocation notes. Provide down guy anchor easement exhibits showing 10-foot width and minimum 5-foot extension from each visible down guy anchor on existing survey.

details.text: Sheet 3, Block 9 (Electric Transmission Notes) indicates transmission structures present on or adjacent to site. Transmission structures often require angled down guy wires extending to ground anchors. Easement exhibit does not show dedicated easement for transmission down guy anchors extending 10 feet either side of guy wire alignment plus minimum 50 feet beyond end of anchor point.

runComments.comment: Sheet 3, Block 9 (Electric Transmission Notes) indicates transmission structures are present on or adjacent to site. Transmission structures often require angled down guy wires extending to ground anchors. Easement exhibit must show dedicated easement for transmission down guy anchors extending 10 feet either side of guy wire alignment plus minimum 50 feet beyond end of anchor point. Verify transmission structure down guy anchor locations and provide transmission guy anchor easement dimensions on plat/easement exhibit.

comments.headline: Privacy fencing clearances from poles and conductors not documented; transmission easement specifications unclear
comments.summary: Landscape plan shows privacy fencing (wooden privacy fences keyed as H.6) on site without dimension callouts showing clearance from outside conductor of overhead electric lines (minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground). Fence posts must maintain minimum 10 feet from utility pole centerlines. Where fencing is within transmission easement, material and grounding specifications required.
comments.crossDep: Transmission line easement location and fencing material specifications require Austin Energy review.
comments.attn: Confirm transmission line easement boundaries on site plan. If fencing is within transmission easement, non-conductive material and grounding requirements apply (UCM § 1.14.0).

details.text: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows wooden privacy fences but provides no clearance dimension callouts from fence faces to outside conductor of overhead electric lines. No dimension annotations demonstrate 7.5-foot minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from outside conductor to fence face and posts.

runComments.comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows fencing (identified by H.6 key notes for wooden privacy fences) but provides no clearance dimension callouts from the fence faces to outside conductor of overhead electric lines. No dimension annotations demonstrate the 7.5-foot minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance. Provide dimension callouts on site plan and fence detail sheets showing clearance from outside conductor to fence face and posts.

details.text: Existing survey (Sheet 4) shows utility pole locations. Landscape plan shows fence alignments. No dimension callouts document horizontal distance from fence posts to existing electric poles. Fence posts must be located minimum 10 feet from pole centerlines.

runComments.comment: Existing survey (Sheet 4) shows utility pole locations. Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows fence alignments. However, no dimension callouts document the horizontal distance from fence posts to existing electric poles. Plans must show that fence posts are located minimum 10 feet from pole centerlines. Provide dimension annotations on site/landscape plan showing distance from each fence post location to nearest utility pole.

details.text: Transmission notes on Sheet 3, Block 9 indicate transmission facilities on or adjacent to site. Landscape plan shows fence alignments but does not clearly show transmission easement boundaries or confirm fence specifications (non-conductive material and grounding) if fencing is located within transmission easement.

runComments.comment: Transmission notes on Sheet 3, Block 9 indicate transmission facilities exist on or adjacent to site, but no clear transmission line routing map is provided showing easement boundaries relative to proposed fencing. Without voltage confirmation and transmission easement delineation, cannot determine whether fences are beneath/within transmission easement and therefore subject to non-conductive material and grounding requirements. Verify transmission line locations, provide transmission easement boundary on site plan, confirm fence specifications (non-conductive material and grounding details) if within easement.

comments.headline: Transformers, lighting, water meters, and site features lack clearance verification
comments.summary: Electrical design plan shows transformer locations but no section views document vertical clearance to overhead lines. Landscape plan shows outdoor lighting but lacks clearance verification. Water meter locations near service drops, trash receptacles, and outdoor fixtures near overhead conductors lack dimension callouts demonstrating 7.5-foot minimum clearances. Permanent building foundations within 5 feet of property line may not allow adequate utility access space.
comments.crossDep: Electrical designer and site engineer coordination on meter/equipment clearances.
comments.attn: Service-mast through-roof installations apply only if roof-mounted masts are proposed; confirm service installation method (overhead mast vs. underground service).

details.text: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer locations. No section views provided showing vertical clearance from top of transformer equipment to overhead electric lines. Transformers must maintain minimum 7.5-foot vertical sky-to-ground clearance from outside conductor.

runComments.comment: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer locations on the site but does not provide section views showing vertical clearance from top of transformer equipment to overhead electric lines. Transformers must maintain minimum 7.5-foot vertical sky-to-ground clearance from outside conductor of overhead lines. Provide section views of transformer locations showing vertical clearance dimension from top of transformer to lowest point of overhead conductor.

details.text: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows decorative outdoor lighting fixtures but does not document clearances from fixture locations to overhead electric conductors. Both 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances must be verified. Site plan notes specify full cut-off, fully shielded fixtures per Land Development Code but do not address overhead clearance.

runComments.comment: Landscape plan shows outdoor lighting fixtures but does not document clearances from these fixtures to overhead electric conductors. Both 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radial clearance must be verified. Site plan notes state decorative lighting must be full cut-off and fully shielded per Land Development Code, but clearance from overhead lines is not addressed. Provide dimension callouts on landscape plan showing clearance from light fixture locations to outside conductor, or provide relocation notes for fixtures within clearance zones.

details.text: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows electrical meter locations. Water meter locations near overhead electric service-drop conductors not documented in relation to overhead service routing. Water meters must maintain minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from outside conductor of service drops.

runComments.comment: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows electrical meter locations but does not document water meter locations relative to overhead electric service-drop conductors. Water meters must maintain minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from outside conductor of service drops. Provide utility plan with water meter locations dimensioned from overhead service-drop routing, or confirm water meters are located clear of service drop conductor zone.

details.text: For 39-unit multi-family project, trash receptacles or enclosures expected on site. Specific locations not clearly documented in relation to overhead electric lines. If trash bins located beneath overhead conductors, raised bins during service collection must maintain minimum 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance from outer conductor.

runComments.comment: For a 39-unit multi-family project, trash receptacles or enclosures are expected but their specific locations are not clearly documented on site plan in relationship to overhead electric lines. If trash bins are located beneath overhead conductors, raised trash bins during service collection must maintain minimum 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance from the outer conductor. Identify trash collection locations on site plan with dimension callouts showing clearance from OHE, or provide notes confirming trash areas are outside the clearance zone.

details.text: Permanent building foundations shown near property line (within 5 feet on some sides). Adequate clearance space must be maintained for electric utility facilities and their future maintenance access adjacent to property boundary where existing electric poles or facilities are located.

runComments.comment: Site plan shows building footprints and property lines. Existing and proposed electric facilities require clearance space in areas adjacent to property. Permanent foundations within 5 feet of property line may not allow necessary clearance space for electric utility facilities and their future maintenance access. Provide dimension annotations on site plan showing distance from building foundation edges to property line, particularly where electric poles or facilities are located adjacent to property boundary, or confirm that adequate clearance space is maintained for utility access.

details.text: For residential service-mast through-roof installations with voltages ≤300V, clearance requirements differ: 3-foot minimum above roof, or 18-inch minimum if mast within 4 feet of roof edge. No building elevation sheets provided showing service-mast through-roof installations. If service masts are proposed through roofs, building elevation sheets must document mast locations and roof clearance dimensions.

runComments.comment: For residential service-mast through-roof installations with voltages ≤300V, clearance requirements differ: 3-foot minimum above roof, or 18-inch minimum if mast is within 4 feet of roof edge. No building elevation sheets showing service-mast through-roof installations have been provided in the site plan package. If service masts are proposed through roofs, building elevation sheets must document mast locations and roof clearance dimensions. If service masts are not used (all underground service), this requirement is not applicable. Clarify service installation method and provide elevation documentation if roof-mounted masts are proposed.

comments.headline: Surveyor mid-span conductor elevations missing; facility-under-OHE prohibition unverified
comments.summary: No registered surveyor mid-span clearance survey data provided showing actual conductor elevations and clearances to buildings, driveways, parking, and other structures. Code contains absolute prohibition on installing customer facilities under or over Austin Energy overhead distribution facilities, distinct from clearance distance requirements. This prohibition not verified with documentation or elevation views. Vertical clearances appear potentially marginal and require professional surveyor verification.
comments.crossDep: Registered professional surveyor engagement; Austin Energy coordination on easement restrictions and facility prohibitions.
comments.attn: Vertical clearances appear marginal based on available estimated line heights and site elevations. Professional surveyor mid-span clearance survey is mandatory before final approval.

details.text: No registered surveyor mid-span clearance data provided showing vertical distance from lowest point of overhead conductors (including attached equipment) to proposed driveways, parking areas, and other site features with height constraints. When vertical clearances appear marginal, registered professional surveyor must provide measured pole and conductor elevation data showing actual mid-span clearances.

runComments.comment: Driveway and parking area elevations are shown on the grading plan. Overhead electric facilities exist on the site. No registered surveyor mid-span clearance measurements are provided showing the vertical distance from the lowest point of overhead conductors (including any attached equipment like transformers) to proposed driveway and parking surface elevations. When vertical clearance appears marginal based on available data, surveyor-certified field measurements of mid-span clearances are required.

Vertical clearances from overhead electric lines to buildings, driveways, and parking areas appear potentially marginal based on site elevations and estimated overhead line heights shown on existing survey. No registered surveyor mid-span clearance survey data is provided. When overhead lines cross or are adjacent to site features with height constraints (driveways requiring 16-18 feet, buildings requiring clearance), a registered professional surveyor must provide measured pole and conductor elevation data showing actual mid-span clearances. Hire registered surveyor to conduct mid-span clearance survey showing actual conductor elevations and clearances to all site features.

Vertical clearance from overhead electric line to proposed driveways appears potentially marginal based on available site elevation data. Registered surveyor survey of pole locations and mid-span clearances is not provided to verify minimum vertical clearance requirements (16-foot or 18-foot) are met.

details.text: UCM § 1.10.3 contains absolute prohibition: customer facilities shall NOT be installed under or over Austin Energy overhead distribution facilities, independent of measured clearance requirements and distinct from clearance distance thresholds. Electric easements shown on site plan (5-foot electric easements and 7.5-foot PUE per plat); buildings and structures shown in proximity. Plans must affirmatively demonstrate that no buildings, building projections, overhangs, or permanent structures are positioned directly beneath or above overhead distribution conductor routing. No clearance verification or facility-exclusion documentation provided.

runComments.comment: Electric easements (5-foot electric easements and 7.5-foot PUE per plat dedication) are shown on site plan. Overhead distribution facilities exist within and adjacent to these easement areas. Site features (buildings, walls, parking) are shown in proximity to these easements, but clearance dimensions from the outside conductor to items within the easement are not provided. The absolute prohibition against facilities under or over distribution lines, as distinct from the 7.5-foot clearance requirement, cannot be verified without elevation data showing vertical spatial relationships.

UCM § 1.10.3 contains an absolute prohibition: customer facilities shall NOT be installed under or over Austin Energy overhead distribution facilities, distinct from the clearance distance requirements and independent of measured clearance. Existing survey shows OHE lines; site plan shows buildings and structures in proximity. Plans must affirmatively demonstrate that no buildings, building projections, overhangs, or other permanent structures are positioned directly beneath or above the overhead distribution conductor routing. Any facility within electric easement must maintain 7.5-foot clearance. Provide clearance verification on all plan sheets showing OHE routing relative to structures.

Site plan shows electric easements (5-foot electric easements from Mecey Subdivision plat recorded as C8S-75-160) but provides no documentation of compliance with the prohibition on installing customer facilities under or over overhead distribution facilities. Code requires absolute prohibition of structures within electric easements (separate from clearance distance requirements). No clearance verification or facility-exclusion documentation provided.

This note is not present on the cover sheet or general notes sheets. Review of Sheets 1 and 3 found no such notification requirement. Add a general note on cover sheet stating: 'Owner/Contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before commencement of any work near high-voltage overhead electric lines per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003.'

However, this note is limited to transmission facilities and does not apply to the distribution line shown on the site plan.
